narrative:
Peter Holden (DOB 05/06/1967, retired) and Lynette Holden (DOB 11/05/1967, working full-time in administration at Shorrock-Browne Medical, ~$20,000 p.a. + 12% SG) are a married couple seeking retirement-focused advice. They own their home (~$2,200,000, Joint) and an investment property (~$2,000,000, Joint — retained/scoped out), and hold ~$2,000,000 cash on hand (Joint). Peter has ~$1,909,603 in Australian Retirement Trust Super Savings; Lynette ~$99,538 (same fund). Living expenses ~$133,400 p.a.
Goals: feel confident their wealth supports their desired lifestyle throughout retirement; draw a reliable, tax-effective retirement income of $140,000 p.a. ($11,667/month) for life; maximise super before retirement; minimise tax; keep estate planning current; remain flexible. Peter is retired; Lynette is undecided on her retirement timeframe and wants flexibility. Both assessed as a Growth risk profile.
Please prepare the SOA per the strategies below: establish a Joint Hub24 investment account and new Hub24 super accounts on the CARE philosophy, close & fully roll over the ART accounts, one-off NCC/recontribution strategy (Peter $130,000; Lynette $390,000 bring-forward), and transition to account-based pension around age 60 drawing a combined ~$140,000 p.a.
notesBudget: Total living expenses ~$133,400 p.a.; desired retirement income $140,000 p.a. ($11,667/month). Cashflow to fund strategy from $2,000,000 cash: less CGT & tax payable ~$223,591; less upfront advice fee from cashflow $1,014; less maximise concessional (FY26) ~$57,600; less NCC (FY27 — Peter $130,000 + Lynette $390,000) $520,000; less 12 months living expenses $140,000; less upfront investment $800,000. Remaining cash ~$257,794 to be retained in a high-interest savings account as a buffer. Estimated combined super balance ~$2,745,000 in 12 months; combined starting benefits to draw income from ~$3,604,639 (today's dollars). Projection assumptions: inflation 2.5%, average return 6.40%.
scopeOther: Specific residential property advice (must be provided by a licensed property agent); personal protection and cashflow/budgeting scoped out at client request given proximity to retirement; estate planning (binding death nominations & Will/POA review) addressed within the superannuation recommendations.
